strengths: Clear problem motivation with compelling visual examples of AR sampling failures on predefined camera trajectories
Clever technical insight that Diffusion Forcing models already provide necessary affordances for stitching without custom training
Training-free approach provides immediate practical value for existing deployed models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with well-designed benchmark, multiple metrics, and thorough ablations demonstrating component contributions
Principled approach to temporal consistency through Omni Guidance that steers joint distribution toward desired conditional distribution
Good presentation with clear figures, pseudocode, and detailed experimental setup
weaknesses: Critically limited evaluation scope: all experiments on single Diffusion Forcing backbone (RealEstate10K). No evaluation on other DF models or recent video models (Runway, Luma, Google DeepMind), making generalization claims unfounded

Significant unaddressed limitations severely restrict practical applicability: external image conditioning fails (Appendix C.1), cannot handle wide-baseline viewpoints (C.2), cannot distinguish structurally similar trajectory segments (C.3)

Limited novelty: core stitching concept well-established; main contribution is recognizing existing DF affordances—more observation than novel technique. Omni Guidance is reasonable but not particularly novel relative to existing guidance methods

Weak theoretical justification: derivation from Eq. 5→6 lacks clear justification; merging γ₁, γ₂ into single γ appears ad-hoc. No principled explanation of why this guidance form is optimal for DF models

Hyperparameter sensitivity inadequately analyzed: default settings (η=0.9, γ=1.0) produce oversmoothed results on some trajectories (Figs. 4, 6); task-specific tuning required without clear guidelines for new trajectories

Loop-closing mechanism appears hand-crafted: requires manually designing spatial context windows per trajectory type (Fig. 8); Impossible Staircase needs special modifications (A.2); unclear how to generalize to arbitrary real-world trajectories
Missing computational cost analysis despite multiple context windows and cyclic conditioning likely increasing computation significantly
No human evaluation for generative task; some metrics (IQ, AQ) slightly favor baselines despite visual superiority claims

Baseline comparisons limited: StochSync repurposed from panorama generation (may be suboptimal); different guidance scales used without justification; no comparison with other recent long-video methods
Contradictory claims: Section 3.5 acknowledges method lacks global receptive field in practice, contradicting earlier theoretical reasoning

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly identifies genuine limitation of AR video generation (inability to anticipate future camera positions) with compelling empirical examples
Elegant core insight: discovers that Diffusion Forcing models already provide necessary affordances for stitching, enabling training-free approach with existing models
Technically sound solution progression: vanilla GVS → stochasticity → Omni Guidance → cyclic conditioning, with each component addressing identified weaknesses
Comprehensive evaluation: multiple metrics (F2FC, LRC, CA, IQ, AQ), thorough ablations (Tables 2-3), qualitative comparisons demonstrating clear improvements over baselines
Excellent presentation: clear writing with effective figures and Algorithm 1 providing implementation clarity
Practical utility: training-free approach immediately deployable with existing DF models without requiring retraining
Honest limitations discussion: thorough appendices (C.1-C.3) transparently document failure modes
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: single backbone model (8-frame DF-Transformer on RealEstate10K), no evaluation across architectures/datasets/models, generalization assumed but untested
Significant failure modes: external image conditioning propagates poorly (C.1), complete failure on wide-baseline viewpoints (C.2), structural ambiguity issues (C.3)—these are not minor edge cases

Incomplete baseline comparison: StochSync designed for images not videos (design mismatch), AR augmented with memory retrieval conflating two separate issues, missing comparisons with other non-autoregressive approaches

Theoretical justifications incomplete: claim that DF enables stitching lacks rigorous justification, jump from Eq. 3 to vanilla GVS unclear, Omni Guidance derivation involves non-obvious approximations (Eq. 5→8 simplification merges heterogeneous terms)

Hyperparameter sensitivity unexplored: multiple hyperparameters (η, γ, overlap, chunk size), η=0.9 appears arbitrary, no sensitivity analysis, different trajectories may require different settings but not systematically studied
Missing computational analysis: no runtime/memory cost comparisons, scalability with video length unclear, practical feasibility for interactive applications not addressed

Moderate novelty: stitching itself established, maximum stochasticity from StochSync, Omni Guidance somewhat incremental over classifier-free guidance, primary contribution is architectural adaptation
Model dependency: strong reliance on backbone training (RE10K biases toward small baselines), wide-baseline failure stems from backbone limitations, generalization to other models unvalidated
Metric limitations: MEt3R for consistency may not capture semantic coherence, VBench IQ/AQ designed for general quality not camera-guided generation, no human evaluation
Limited problem analysis: cyclic conditioning for loop closing presented ad-hoc without principled spatial window selection algorithm, requires manual specification per trajectory

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical applications (cinematography, autonomous driving synthetic data); visual demonstrations effectively show autoregressive sampling failures
Clever technical insight: Diffusion Forcing's per-token noise capability already enables stitching without custom training, making this training-free method immediately applicable to existing models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple challenging trajectories, quantitative metrics spanning consistency/collision/quality, extensive ablations on key components, and testing across three backbone architectures
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figs. 1, 6, 7) and detailed specification (Algorithm 1), supporting reproducibility with implementation details and hyperparameters
Honest discussion of limitations with root cause analysis in Appendix C rather than dismissal, including wide-baseline failures, external conditioning issues, and manual window definition constraints
Strong empirical results: significant improvements over baselines in frame-to-frame consistency (F2FC), long-range consistency (LRC), and collision avoidance (CA) on diverse camera trajectories
weaknesses: Severely limited applicability: requires complete future camera trajectory in advance, making the method inapplicable to interactive/streaming scenarios—a fundamental constraint that excludes real-time applications

Critical scalability limitation: spatial neighbors in cyclic conditioning must be manually defined per trajectory (Fig. 8), preventing generalization to arbitrary camera paths; proposed learning-based solution left to future work

Theoretical-practical gap in loop closing: Section 3.5 claims 'global context' via growing receptive field, yet Fig. 4 empirically shows this insufficient without explicit loop closing; theory does not explain why cyclic conditioning works

Omni Guidance derivation lacks rigor: transition from Eq. 4→8 merges guidance terms without formal justification; claim of being 'generalization of Fractional History Guidance' unproven; breaks standard classifier-free guidance assumptions without rigorous theoretical grounding

Multiple unresolved failure modes: (1) wide-baseline viewpoints fail completely (Figs. 13-14) due to backbone training on small viewpoint shifts; (2) external image conditioning fails to propagate context frames beyond a few timesteps (Fig. 12); (3) structurally similar camera segments cause spurious detail generation

Video quality degradation in key scenarios: Table 1 shows IQ/AQ metrics sometimes favor baselines (e.g., Panorama 2-loop AQ: 0.376 vs AR 0.422); quality-consistency Pareto frontier not fully characterized

Limited technical novelty: combines existing techniques (diffusion stitching from CompDiffuser/StochSync, stochasticity from StochSync, guidance from classifier-free/Inner Guidance); main contribution is applying to video via DF observation, which is incremental

Restricted evaluation scope: only RealEstate10K-derived models tested despite introduction mentioning Kong, Google DeepMind, Runway, Luma models; no real-world video evaluation; collision detection uses inferred rather than ground truth depth

Memory scaling concerns: parallel diffusion window processing increases memory requirements compared to sequential AR; 'scalable implementation' barely specified; for very long sequences, feasibility remains unclear

Incomplete ablations: no systematic study of Omni Guidance formulation alternatives; missing interaction analysis between loop closing and guidance at different stochasticity levels; stochasticity selection lacks principled guidelines
